text:
sarah: Thanks for joining the Q&A follow-up thread — quick clarifications from today's all-hands about release cadence, oncall, and quality bars. Drop short questions and we'll answer sequentially.
jon: Quick one — are we moving to a fixed 2-week release cadence or staying flexible?
anya: Also curious about how hotfixes fit into that cadence.
leo: And how do rollouts map to Dedicated vs Hosted environments?
maria: Plus: what counts as a quality gate before a production rollout?
sarah: Short answers: cadence = target biweekly for minor releases, quarterly for major platform changes. Hotfixes still go out ad-hoc; we have a separate fastpath. Dedicated/Hosted follow same rollout policy but different traffic cutover thresholds. Quality gate = green CI, no critical SLO regressions in staging, and at least one feature-flagged canary run.
jon: Can you expand on "fastpath" hotfixes? Who approves?
sarah: Fastpath = emergency hotfix workflow: oncall owns initial triage + patch, eng-sre reviews within 30m, exec approval only for cross-region DB changes. We log everything in the incident channel.
eng-ops-bot: Reminder: fastpath checklist: 1) minimal diff 2) automated tests pass 3) canary run 4) rollback plan documented.
anya: For canaries — what % traffic do we use? Is it different on Dedicated?
leo: Related: how long do canaries run before ramp?
sarah: Default canary = 1% for 15 minutes with automated health checks. If metrics stable, we 10x every 15m until 100%. Dedicated customers may opt for slower ramps via config.
maria: What are the SLO thresholds we gate on for releases?
jon: And who signs off on performance regressions?
sarah: We gate on 99th latency and error rate: no more than 10% relative regression on P99 and <0.1% increase in user-visible 5xxs for infra releases. Perf regressions require research lead + eng-ops signoff.
anya: How strict is the code freeze period before quarterly releases?
leo: Do feature branches stay open?
sarah: Code freeze = 72 hours for the core runtime ahead of major release. Exceptions are small perf/security fixes via fastpath. Feature branches should be merged to main before freeze or feature-flagged if the work is still ongoing.
maria: Are oncall rotations changing? We had some confusion post-all-hands.
jon: Specifically the weekend overlap window?
eng-ops-bot: Oncall rota update: weekly rotations remain, handover window moves to 60 minutes. Weekend overlap window = 2 hours on Friday into Saturday during high-deploy weeks.
sarah: We're keeping weekly rotations but adding a secondary oncall for high-traffic launches (opt-in; rotation managed by eng-ops).
leo: How do SLAs map to internal SLOs? If a customer-facing SLA is threatened, what's the escalation path?
sarah: SLA incidents escalate to SRE lead -> head of product -> CTO. Internal SLOs are monitored continuously; if error budget burn >50% in a 24h window, auto-alert to PagerDuty and we pause non-critical rollouts.
anya: Pause rollouts automatically? Who can unpause?
sarah: Unpause requires eng-ops + release manager signoff after the burn rate normalizes and root cause mitigated.
maria: Any change in PR review SLAs? We saw longer queues.
jon: Wonder if we can adopt a hard 48-hour reviewer SLA for critical repos.
sarah: New guideline: critical repos = 48h review target; platform infra = 72h. We'll track via CODEOWNERS and a weekly digest to leads.
leo: Will there be a dashboard for rollout status and rollback history?
eng-ops-bot: New rollout dashboard planned — includes canary metrics, rollout stage, and last 30 rollback events. ETA: end of next sprint.
anya: For teams: recommended checklist for every release?
sarah: Use this minimal checklist before creating a release PR:
```
- CI green
- Perf smoke in staging
- Feature flags for behavioral changes
- Rollout plan + abort criteria
- Owner + oncall notified
```
maria: Nice. One last ask: can we get a summary doc with timelines and the updated oncall rota?
sarah: Yes — I'll ask eng-ops to publish a short doc and a calendar export by EOD tomorrow. Thanks everyone, keep questions coming here. :thumbsup:
